recognize_zh: MPO 細胞化學染色中，左下與中央的顆粒球細胞質呈棕色陽性，右側一顆核過度分葉的嗜中性球細胞質卻完全淡染無棕色顆粒，代表這顆發育異常的嗜中性球 MPO 陰性。
features: Myeloperoxidase cytochemistry on peripheral blood with blue nuclear counterstain
Neutrophil on the right with multiple (hypersegmented) nuclear lobes and pale cytoplasm lacking brown MPO reaction product
Adjacent granulocytes (center and lower left) show brown granular MPO positivity as internal positive controls
Unstained red cells in the background, some with target-like central pallor
describe_en: Myeloperoxidase cytochemical stain of a peripheral blood smear shows granulocytes with strong brown granular cytoplasmic positivity, serving as internal positive controls. In contrast, a neutrophil with abnormal nuclear hypersegmentation shows complete absence of MPO reaction product in its cytoplasm. In a patient with a myelodysplastic neoplasm, findings are consistent with acquired MPO deficiency in dysplastic neutrophils.

ddx.vs: Inherited MPO deficiency affects essentially all neutrophils uniformly, whereas here MPO-negative neutrophils coexist with normally positive granulocytes.
Those cells have non-lobated nuclei, whereas this MPO-negative cell has a multilobed neutrophil nucleus.
Megaloblastic neutrophils are hypersegmented but retain normal MPO activity, so MPO loss favors a clonal dysplastic process.
